method: Five parallel agents scanned every page (generated HTML, builders, data, diagrams) for overlap that should collapse to ONE canonical home. SCOPED to wiki HTML pages & diagrams — the numbered spec spine (Docs 01–19 markdown) is OUT of scope: where a page restates a spec, the fix edits the PAGE (point at the spec), never the spec. Pure spec↔spec and source-data overlaps are listed at the bottom as out-of-scope. PLAN ONLY — nothing is merged until you approve a candidate by id.
framing: Scoped to the wiki surface you actually manage: the generated HTML pages and the diagrams. Most apparent duplication is intentional, already single-sourced data-driven VIEWS. The real page-level hazard is narrower: (a) generated pages that hand-copy tables instead of rendering from the canonical JSON; (b) framing/boilerplate restated across sibling pages; (c) a few pages that restate a spec's content (fixed by editing the page to point at the spec). Risk here is small: low = generated-page render / label cleanup; med = a standalone page or one that must preserve cross-refs / a diagram-data guard. Nothing in this scoped view edits the spec spine.

findings.title: Generated pages hand-copy the pillar/weights/constants tables
findings.overlap: The pillar roster, base weights W_k, and the scoring-constants table are hand-listed in these generated pages instead of rendered from the canonical JSON (pillars.json / pillar-weights.json / constants.json) — exactly the drift the JSON-canonical rule (D32) exists to prevent (admin-weights vs Doc 03 drift is already a flagged risk).
findings.canonical: the data/*.json (already canonical); these pages should be VIEWS of it.
findings.mechanism: render-from-JSON (replace the hand-authored tables in the builders)
findings.gain: Removes 2–3 hand-copies of each numeric table; kills the known overview/admin-weights drift.

findings.title: Wearable trust-tier (D22) table re-tabled on 3 pages
findings.overlap: The D22 three-tier table / tier chips are re-tabled on both baseline pages as well as the wearables catalog; the values still await calibration, so the copies will silently desync.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (the baseline pages cite it instead of re-tabling)
findings.gain: One update site for the tier values.

findings.title: Gaps/review pages: framing restated on all 4
findings.overlap: Five genuinely distinct axes (app surface / buildability / cohesion / coverage / red-team) — NOT content duplicates. But the axis legend, the 'Illustrative §5.6' callout, and the 4×4 sibling cross-ref scaffolding are restated on every page.
findings.canonical: chapter-7 landing owns the 5-axis legend; a shared builder snippet owns the callout + sibling block.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (consolidate the framing; do NOT merge the views)
findings.gain: One home for the taxonomy framing.

findings.title: uber-map vs calc-uber — naming collision (not a dup)
findings.overlap: Distinct artifacts (live Calculation Explorer vs static 5-view architecture diagram), but index.html lists uber-map TWICE under two names and the two titles are confusingly similar.
findings.mechanism: label cleanup (dedupe the index cards; give distinct one-line descriptors)
findings.gain: Removes the strongest 'are these the same page?' confusion.

sections.title: Low risk — generated pages / data behind pages

findings.title: Onboarding gating vs Eligibility & gating
findings.overlap: Both explain how onboarding answers gate downstream questions (both read question-bank.json gating metadata).
findings.canonical: eligibility-gating owns the gating-rule semantics; onboarding keeps only the first-run sequence/UX.
findings.gain: Removes the double-explanation of the same gating mechanism.

findings.title: feedback-loop hard-codes its action list
findings.overlap: The demo's 5 ACTIONS are hard-coded inline; engine constants are already sourced from PURESCORE_DATA, the action list is not.
findings.canonical: the canonical action library (same data the calculator reads).
findings.mechanism: fold (data-source the demo's action subset, like the constants)
findings.gain: Demo labels/effects can't drift from the library.

findings.title: chapter-0 landing ≈ index.html
findings.overlap: chapter-0 (Start-here landing) is a thin auto-generated subset of what index.html does richer — two 'Start here' homes.
findings.mechanism: point chapter-0 at index, or slim it (the one landing that competes with Home)

findings.title: SI-units blurb duplicated
findings.overlap: The SI unit-conversion explanation appears on both pages (both over units.json).
findings.gain: One home for the units blurb.

findings.title: Persona attributes duplicated behind the two persona pages
findings.overlap: The 13 clinical personas' attributes (age/meds/multipliers/notes) are stored in BOTH personas.json and persona-matrix.json behind these two pages.
findings.canonical: personas.json owns persona attributes; the matrix references ids + owns only the inference layer.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (de-dup the data; keep both pages)
findings.gain: One edit site for persona attributes.

findings.title: Two 'coverage' surfaces with near-identical names
findings.overlap: production-gaps embeds a 'Clinical coverage register' (coverage.json) while appendix-coverage-audit covers the questionnaire loop — adjacent 'what's missing' surfaces with confusingly similar names in one chapter.
findings.mechanism: rename the production-gaps section + point to coverage-audit
findings.gain: Stops the two reading as duplicates.

sections.title: Medium risk — a page restates a spec (edit the PAGE, never the spec)

findings.title: purescore-sex restates Doc 08 bands
findings.overlap: The sex page restates Doc 08's reference cut-points (Total-T, HDL-M/F, waist, FSH/AMH…) as a male/female toggle; its unique value is the toggle UI + the gated-question list (6 male + 21 female).
findings.canonical: Doc 08 owns the bands (do NOT edit the spec).
findings.mechanism: edit the PAGE: replace restated bands with a Doc 08 pointer (or generate them from the same band data); keep the toggle + gated questions
findings.gain: One place to re-verify sex bands.

findings.title: class-model (object) vs dossier-erd (entity) can desync
findings.overlap: dossier-erd is 'one table per class' over the same class spec class-model renders; per-class field lists are restated, so a field change needs two edits.
findings.canonical: class-model is the object-model source; ERD is a downstream view.
findings.mechanism: single-spec guard: verify build_grid_erd generates FROM the class spec, not a parallel hand-list (no page merge)
findings.gain: Prevents field-level drift between the two diagrams.

findings.title: Care pages restate Doc 11 §9 delivery / Doc 16 §2 escalation
findings.overlap: prevention-engagement restates the Doc 11 §9 delivery mechanism (the page itself says reminders should route through §9) and care escalation restates Doc 16 §2 tiers + the PHQ-9→C-SSRS gate. The 3 care pages among themselves are NOT duplicates.
findings.canonical: Doc 11 §9 (delivery) / Doc 16 §2 (escalation) — do NOT edit the specs.
findings.mechanism: edit the PAGES: express reminders as content/triggers + reference §9/§2 instead of restating
findings.gain: No parallel sender/escalation spec to drift.

findings.title: consent-onboarding doesn't cite Doc 16 §4
findings.overlap: The standalone consent prototype enacts exactly Doc 16 §4's policy (granular consent, genetic/reproductive, withdrawal, audit) but doesn't visibly cite it as its spec.
findings.mechanism: edit the PAGE: add an 'implements Doc 16 §4' binding line; align its data classes to §4 1:1 (standalone page — not regenerated)
findings.gain: Prototype can't silently drift from the governing policy.

findings.title: The 3 care pages among themselves

findings.title: Admin set / thin dossiers / chapter landings / purescore-system
findings.overlap: Each is a distinct surface / altitude / diagram type; landings are generated from NAV (editing NAV propagates).
